page: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by a 64-bit x86 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, presenting 2 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading. Hardware cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Supported CPU instructions encompass AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic primitives such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance provides 16.0 GB of memory, equating to an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is provisioned, requiring remote block storage for persistence, and the configuration contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight standard single-threaded execution balanced against throughput limitations inherent to a 2-vCPU layout. The processor registered a stress-ng single-core score of 1890.78, a Geekbench single-core score of 1623.0, and single-threaded gzip compression at 28.45 GB/sec. In contrast, parallel compute scores reflect lower overall tiers, with stress-ng multi-core reaching 1932.89 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 1880.0. Memory bandwidth was benchmarked at 15.07 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 13.81 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, the system demonstrated 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The hardware composition provides an efficient qualitative footprint when applications demand elevated memory capacity relative to compute capacity. Rather than paying for surplus processor cores, systems requiring memory headroom benefit from the 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile suits low-concurrency workloads that exceed typical general-purpose memory footprints, such as lightweight relational databases, small in-memory key-value stores, intermediate caching layers, and staging environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached block storage, and does not contain a discrete GPU. In performance testing, the instance records intermediate single-thread performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1623.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1890.78. Because compute capacity is limited to 2 vCPUs, multi-core and database benchmarks reflect lower comparative percentiles, showing 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance provides an efficient profile for memory-sensitive, low-concurrency tasks such as small database instances, in-memory caches, and background processing services.
